reviewScope: Independent chapter-one descriptions, contracts, algorithm bodies in all five languages, worked traces, and standalone test adapters. This records an actual content review, not a presence-check result.

questions.algorithm: Fixed ASCII presence flags; reject at the second occurrence.
questions.review: The empty case, case significance, null character, fixed alphabet, invariant and early return agree across all five implementations.
questions.relatedExisting: blind75_contains_duplicate operates on integer arrays; no exact callable alias is claimed.

questions.algorithm: Equal-length check, add first-string counts, subtract second-string counts and reject negative supply.
questions.review: Multiplicity and all ASCII units are significant. Equal total length makes a final all-zero scan unnecessary. The five implementations all apply the same argument.
questions.relatedExisting: blind75_valid_anagram has a narrower lowercase-letter contract; this ASCII exercise is staged separately.

questions.algorithm: Backward expansion in a supplied character buffer with exact final capacity.
questions.review: The read character is saved before writes; output never overwrites an earlier unread cell. The implementation uses capacity rather than a counting pass, and its complexity wording was corrected accordingly.
questions.bankChoice: Exact rather than merely sufficient capacity removes trailing-output ambiguity. trueLength is authoritative, including original trailing spaces. The callable returns void; the adapter observes the same buffer.

questions.algorithm: Fold ASCII uppercase letters, ignore nonletters, count odd letter frequencies.
questions.review: The public Common.java establishes letter filtering and case normalization. These differ from existing exact-character palindrome-permutation problems. All five algorithms use 128 counters with only lowercase-letter slots populated.
questions.bankChoice: ASCII domain makes the letter-unit policy consistent across languages; punctuation-only input retains zero letters and returns true.

questions.algorithm: Two pointers; the first mismatch skips the longer side or advances both when lengths match.
questions.review: The used-edit flag allows zero edits, rejects a second mismatch, handles either argument being longer and permits one unmatched final character. A transposition is not incorrectly treated as a single edit.

questions.algorithm: Enumerate maximal runs, build letter/count candidate, keep it only for a strict length reduction.
questions.review: All five implementations distinguish runs from global counts, retain the original on a tie, handle empty input, and use decimal counts with multiple digits.

languageDetails.javascript: Collect letter/count strings and join once; no repeated growing-string concatenation.
languageDetails.python: Collect pieces and join once; no repeated growing-string concatenation.
languageDetails.cpp: Append to std::string; the linear-time description uses amortized string growth.

questions.algorithm: Transpose above the diagonal, then reverse each row by swapping cells.
questions.review: The coordinate proof (r,c) -> (c,r) -> (c,n-1-r) matches every implementation. No row reference is replaced. Mutation adapters observe row identity, not just final cell values.
questions.bankChoice: An empty square matrix is an explicit no-op. The public reference method reports false for empty input; this bank's void callable documents its empty-input convention rather than silently claiming an identical callable.
questions.relatedExisting: blind75_rotate_image has the same core rotation task. Separate CtCI references and explicit contracts avoid changing existing progress or drafts.

questions.algorithm: Discover zero rows/columns before mutation, then clear their union.
questions.review: Every language separates discovery from writing, so newly created zeroes cannot cascade. Rectangular, zero-column and empty matrices are handled. The complexity bound includes row scanning when the column count is zero.
questions.relatedExisting: blind75_set_matrix_zeroes shares the core task; this staged contract additionally makes empty dimensions and row-identity observations explicit.

questions.algorithm: Reject empty or unequal-length inputs, then search second once in first+first.
questions.review: All five implementations make exactly one search call and use positive equal lengths. A permutation alone is insufficient. The complexity explanation deliberately leaves the runtime substring-search cost explicit instead of asserting an unsupported universal linear bound.
questions.bankChoice: Two empty inputs return false, as in the examined public Java implementation.

languageBindingReview.csharp: ASCII char values index fixed arrays; strings are immutable. Mutable char[] and int[][] arguments are checked after calls. StringComparison.Ordinal is used for rotation search.
languageBindingReview.javascript: ASCII charCodeAt and one-character array cells implement the declared units. Integer counts stay far below Number's exact range. Matrix rows and the character buffer remain original objects.
languageBindingReview.python: ord operates only on declared ASCII input; lists represent mutable characters and matrix rows. Slice copies are avoided in the actual one-edit solution; oracle edit enumeration is separate.
languageBindingReview.cpp: String inputs are const references; mutable vectors are references. ASCII preconditions prevent signed-char indexing issues. Matrix row storage is observed to detect replacement allocations. No user algorithms are executed during source generation.
languageBindingReview.java: String.charAt uses the same units under the ASCII contract. Arrays have fixed lengths and row identities are observed. StringBuilder is used for run encoding. The independently authored sources compile under Java 21.
